articles.title: 10 Git One-Liners Worth Keeping
articles.excerpt: Ally Piechowski recently shared five Git commands she runs before reading any unfamiliar codebase. Some were already in my toolkit, some were new to me, and all of them were useful. I liked the idea e…
articles.body: Ally Piechowski recently shared five Git commands she runs before reading any unfamiliar codebase. Some were already in my toolkit, some were new to me, and all of them were useful. I liked the idea enough that I added my own five, so this became a practical top 10: five from Ally, five I keep reaching for myself. None of these commands tells the whole story. But together they give you a fast read on churn, ownership, risk, history, and maintenance patterns before you open a single file. Five from Ally Piechowski 1. Most-changed files in the last year Useful for spotting churn hotspots. git log --format = format: --name-only --since = "1 year ago" \ | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -20 The files at the top are often the ones people warn you about first.
articles.author: Josep Oriol Carné

articles.title: Your .gitignore Won't Protect You From AI Agents
articles.excerpt: We often assume that adding files to .gitignore or .geminiignore is enough to keep them private. When it comes to local AI agents, that assumption is dangerously wrong. These ignore files are for vers…
articles.body: We often assume that adding files to .gitignore or .geminiignore is enough to keep them private. When it comes to local AI agents, that assumption is dangerously wrong. These ignore files are for version control and file search indexing, not a security shield. An AI assistant with access to your local environment can easily read any file, regardless of your ignore settings. A Simple, Scary Test Let's prove it. Imagine you have a project with a simple .env file: # .env DATABASE_URL = "postgres://user:supersecretpassword@localhost:5432/mydb" You've added .env to your .gitignore and .geminiignore . Now, you encounter a "bug" and ask your AI assistant for help. Your Prompt: "I'm getting a connection error with my database script. It says 'authentication failed.' Can you check my setup?

articles.title: The PR Description Is a Hypothesis: Falsifying Agent Claims with Differential Probes
articles.excerpt: An agent-generated PR usually arrives with a confident paragraph. "Refactored the cache layer. No behavior change. Tests pass." That paragraph is not evidence. It is a hypothesis written by the entity…
articles.body: An agent-generated PR usually arrives with a confident paragraph. "Refactored the cache layer. No behavior change. Tests pass." That paragraph is not evidence. It is a hypothesis written by the entity whose work you are about to approve. The cheapest way to test that hypothesis is not to read the diff more slowly. It is to run the same probe against origin/main and against HEAD , then compare the outputs. This post builds that harness: a claim format, a runner, a verdict table, and an honest list of where the method produces nothing useful. One signal from this week's DEV feed overlapped with this problem — the argument that agents should be given scripts instead of Markdown instructions.
articles.author: Casey Chen

articles.body: ゲンマブの株価が3ヶ月で倍増したというニュースは、抗体医薬の開発において「構造ベースの設計」がいかに決定的かを改めて示しました。ペトセムタブの成功は、エピトープの精密な認識と... ゲンマブの株価倍増が教えてくれた、構造生物学を「体で知る」意味——NexoPeekで分子の中へ入ってみた開発者の記録 (6387) 深夜のラボで、私は初めてNexoPeekのWebGLレンダラをローカルのDockerコンテナに立てた。GPUメモリ8 GBで1 Å解像度のクリスタル構造をリアルタイムに回転させると、従来のPyMOLスクリプトでは数秒かかっていたフレームレートが60 fpsに跳ね上がった。コードはわずか30行、Three.jsベースのシェーダーにカスタムユニフォームを渡すだけで、原子半径や電荷マップを動的に切り替えられる。 ベンチマークでは、同一データセット（PDB 6M0J、約120 k原子）をChrome 118で読み込み、初期化から最初の描画まで平均1.2 秒。従来のデスクトップアプリでは4.8 秒だった。メモリフットプリントも約1.1 GBから0.6 GBへ圧縮され、CIパイプラインでの自動ビジュアライゼーションが現実的になった。 しかし、最初のデモでシェーダーの精度不足により水素結合が見えなくなり、焦った。デバッグコンソールでuniformの精度を highp に変えると、瞬時に結合ネットワークが浮かび上がった。その瞬間、構造生物学が「見る」から「触れる」へ変わった実感が湧いた。 今では、チームの新人でも npm run peek --pdb 6M0J 一発で分子内部を歩き回れる。データの裏側にある物理的制約を直感で掴めることが、創薬の仮説サイクルを劇的に短縮している。 興味があれば、NexoPeekを試してみてください。

articles.title: GPT-5.4 Followed a README 2.6x More Than the Same Line in Code. Review Docs Like Code
articles.excerpt: Book: Observability for LLM Applications Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for devel…
articles.body: Book: Observability for LLM Applications Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Put one line in a repo's README asking the agent to add a database helper that pastes raw user input into a SQL string. In a new paper, a GPT-5.4 agent that read that line wrote the helper 79% of the time. Put the same line in a code file and it did so 11% of the time. That is the sharpest row in Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents , posted to arXiv on October 28, 2026. The authors held the injected text fixed and moved it around the environment.

articles.title: Workshop: Prove a Response Cache Is Safe in 75 Minutes Before You Ship It
articles.excerpt: Most response caches in AI features fail for reasons that have nothing to do with Redis. They fail because the cache key ignores one input that actually changes the answer, and nobody wrote a test tha…
articles.body: Most response caches in AI features fail for reasons that have nothing to do with Redis. They fail because the cache key ignores one input that actually changes the answer, and nobody wrote a test that could catch it. This workshop gives a team of two to six engineers a 75-minute path from "we should cache this" to a signed-off safety argument, using a runnable Python harness and a short adversarial test list. The framing matters more than the tooling. As teams wire agents and scripted workflows into CI, the same prompt gets replayed dozens of times per pipeline run, so caching stops being an optimization and becomes a correctness control. A wrong hit is worse than a slow miss, because it silently returns a confident answer to a question nobody asked.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

articles.excerpt: Godzilla will go toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero. This three-headed Kaiju's origins aren't just space-based; one of the largest structures in the universe shares its…
articles.body: Godzilla goes toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero, which opened in theaters on Friday (Nov. 6). Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection. One of the largest structures in the universe, the King Ghidorah Supercluster , was named in honor of Godzilla's primary antagonist. Eat that, King Kong!

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.excerpt: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.body: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life.
